sources.note: Nothing; administrative name-change request. Text kept only in the work dir (), not in the held dir, since it is not about Liki.

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1981. Retention and innovation in Sarmic language[s]: Reflexes of POC *ŋm. Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya 9(3): 35-42. (Glottolog ref 691707, listed by Glottolog as a comparative study; cited in Glottolog's subclassification comment for Liki.)
sources.note: Nothing for Liki. The paper treats reflexes of POC *ŋm and Sobei vowel changes (vowel shift, penultimate-vowel syncope in trisyllables, *ma- > me-, *p > f) in six Sarmi-coast languages (Sobei, Wakde, Masimasi, Anus, Bonggo, Tarpia); Liki/Moar is not in the data table (p. 36) or anywhere in the text. The only prosodic remark is about Bonggo: 'in BON (4) a fairly common process of lenition of the first vowel took place through apparent destressing' (pp. 36-37). No stress, accent or tone statement for any language.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives record 69262 'Liki Wordlist Sterner' (metadata page)
sources.note: Metadata only (1974-08-16; 4 pp; 74 entries; Language Assessment).

sources.citation: Kafryawan, Wira & Andi Miftahul Maulidil Mursyid (depositors). 2025-2026. The documentation and description of Liki, an Austronesian language of Papua. London: Endangered Languages Archive, deposit 0830 (ELDP grant SG1134). Collection handlehttp://hdl.handle.net/2196/9845fd35-9109-4e1b-a420-5e20430ef56e.Read here: Kafryawan, Wira. 2025. Metadocumentation for Liki language project (5 pp.).
sources.note: The only phonological content is the practical orthography with its grapheme-to-phoneme (IPA) table: vowels a i u e o ə; consonants b, c, d, f, g, h, j /ɟ/, k, kh /x/, l, m, n, ng /ŋ/, ny /ɲ/, p, r, s, sy /ʃ/, t, w, y /j/, z, ' /ʔ/. The template's prompt to describe 'a special convention (such as numbers to indicate tones)' is answered with no such convention, and 'Special annotation conventions: Not applicable'. Nothing on stress, accent, tone or intonation. The deposit title promises a 'description'; none (sketch grammar/phonology) is in the collection as of today.

sources.citation: Kafryawan, Wira (researcher); Loisa Teno & Onesimus Teno (speakers). 2025 [annotation 2026]. Liki wordlist 1 / Daftar kata Liki 1 (ELAR item lio143; file lio143-int_20260801.eaf, interlinearised ELAN export, 411 elicited items: nature, kin, pronouns). In Kafryawan & Mursyid, The documentation and description of Liki, ELAR deposit 0830 / ELDP SG1134.
sources.note: Primary lexical data in the practical orthography (ASCII only; apostrophe = glottal stop, e.g. bo'etate, nena'); no stress marks, accents or tone digits on any of the 411 items (e.g. fendu 'world', selmale 'soil', wane 'sand', salo 'mountain', nensu 'island', rani 'water', matilon 'sea'). Data only; the time-aligned wav/MP4 of this and nine further wordlist sessions are open for anyone wanting to measure stress.

sources.citation: Sterner, Robert H. [& Joyce Sterner]. 1974. Liki Wordlist [Survey word list (standard), 'LIKIWINI (Sobei)', Pulau Liki, 16 Aug 1974, informant Akau Teno]. MS, 4 pp., 74 entries. SIL Language & Culture Archives 69262. (= Glottolog 'Sterner & Sterner 1974 Likiwini')
sources.note: No prose at all, but primary stress is marked (raised vertical stroke) on almost every one of the 74 handwritten phonetic forms; position varies: initial in 'dabu 'head', 'mani 'bird', 'fati 'stone', 'yafu 'fire', 'maros 'sits' but final in tam'tu 'man', mut'ni 'woman', el'we 'dog', sa'lil 'walks', dua'he 'big', nE'tu 'small', ma'do 'moon'; penult/other in longer forms (mE'tarfE 'smoke', tim'pana? 'eats', 'mimbiku 'elbow'). Data only, no rule stated.

sources.citation: Grace, George W. 1970. Notes on the phonological history of the Austronesian languages of the Sarmi Coast. UH Working Papers in Linguistics 2(9): 55-104 (= Oceanic Linguistics 10: 11-37, 1971)
sources.note: Liki/Moar is not among the six vocabularies treated (Sobei, Wakde, Masimasi, Anus, Bonggo, Tarpia); a full-text search for stress/accent Liki/Moar = 0; no stress statement for any language.

sources.citation: de Clercq, F. S. A. 1894. The Western and Northern Coasts of Netherlands New Guinea. In G. G. Batten (transl./ed.), Glimpses of the Eastern Archipelago: ethnographical, geographical, historical, pp. 1-29. Singapore: Singapore and Straits Printing Office. (English translation of de Clercq 1893, TKNAG 2e ser. 10.)
sources.note: No phonology content: ethnographic description of Liki (villages, houses, trade, a dozen cultural vocabulary items such as bamoe 'sago', for 'pig', tori 'temple', sasoea 'arrows', sanef 'bow'), the sentence 'On the islands the same language is spoken with little difference', and numerals 1-5 and 10 for Koemamba, Wakde, Masi-Masi, Jamna. Nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: de Clercq, F. S. A. 1893. De West- en Noordkust van Nederlandsch Nieuw-Guinea (vervolg en slot). Tijdschrift van het Koninklijk Nederlandsch Aardrijkskundig Genootschap, 2e serie, deel X (Meer uitgebreide artikelen): 841-884, 981-1021. Leiden: Brill. (Glottolog ref; Dutch original of A's work 1.) Read on Delpher, volume MMUBA13:001613001, seq 244-273.
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone for the island language: the language paragraph gives only the one-language remark and numerals (Koemamba 1 tes, 2 loe, 3 taoer, 4 faoe, 5 lim [scanned 'Urn'], 10 sinafoen; Wakde, Masi-Masi, Jamna lists) plus scattered cultural vocabulary in the text (bamoe 'sago', niwi 'coconut', sasoea 'arrows', sanef 'bow'). A search of the whole article for klemtoon/klem/nadruk/accent/toon/lettergreep finds only two remarks on the pronunciation of the place names Wandamen and Mamberamo.
